title: Simulation Can Tell You What Your Agents are Actually Doing: A Conversation with Zhou Yu
gist: In an InfoQ Architects Podcast with Michael Stiefel, Columbia professor and Arklex.ai founder Zhou Yu argues that non-deterministic, multi-turn AI agents cannot be evaluated with static reference-based benchmarks and instead need dynamic user simulations with personas, goals, corner cases and multi-metric task verifiers across the whole lifecycle. She claims evaluation spend is flipping from a small QA share to a first-class cost, and that simulation should become a shared engineering platform; note the speaker's company sells such testing tools.

themes.theme: Why static benchmarks fail for agents

insights.claim: Zhou Yu argues AI agents are multi-turn, multi-tool, long-horizon programs whose next user input depends on the agent's previous reply, so static reference-based benchmarks with gold answers break whenever the system changes.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Agent evaluation requires new tooling beyond static benchmarks, creating a market for simulation-based QA.
insights.quote: You can't rely on a static benchmark of what we call reference-based evaluation.
insights.locator: Multi-Turn Agents and Moving Targets

insights.claim: Because natural language input is exponential in complexity and diversity compared to button-driven software, testing conversational agents is far harder than traditional UI testing.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Testing cost scales with the open-endedness of LLM interfaces, burdening agent deployments.
insights.locator: Simulating User Personas

insights.claim: Since agents generate different plans each run, Zhou Yu says evaluation must be integrated goal-completion testing of whether the user's goal was achieved, rather than turn-by-turn checks, using task verifiers that may be rule-based or LLM judges plus safety and alignment checks.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Outcome-based evaluation is becoming the standard metric for production agents.
insights.locator: Goal Completion and Task Verifiers

insights.claim: For critical use cases, Zhou Yu recommends running agent tests multiple times and requiring pass at K, meaning the agent must pass every one of K runs, because of non-determinism.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Reliability testing multiplies compute and evaluation costs for mission-critical agents.
insights.locator: So that's why simulation is important.

insights.claim: Zhou Yu's approach uses agents to simulate user behavior with standardized personas, goals and corner cases, replacing costly real user studies with automated, repeatable CI/CD scenarios.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Simulated users can substitute for expensive human testing, lowering QA costs for agent builders.
insights.locator: So that's why we started looking

insights.claim: Simulated users with known goals solve a problem production data cannot: in production you don't know the user's real intent, e.g. whether an abruptly ended chat meant success or frustration.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Synthetic evaluation provides ground truth that production analytics lack.
insights.quote: If you look at production data, you don't know the real intent behind the user, then it's much more difficult.
insights.locator: If you look at production data

insights.claim: Agent simulation scenarios capture real-user corner cases such as repeated questions, keyboard glitches, accents, acronym use by experienced versus novice users, code switching between languages, and background factory noise.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Coverage of messy real-world inputs is a key differentiator for agent-testing vendors.
insights.locator: So your agent in some way pressure

insights.claim: Scenario inputs for agent simulations can be generated from tool-call trajectories, existing customer-service data, product design docs, prior user studies, domain knowledge and even mined social media, with subject-matter experts reviewing and editing them in natural language.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Human SMEs remain in the loop, limiting full automation of agent QA.
insights.locator: Designing, Running, Maintaining Simulation Tests

insights.claim: Zhou Yu argues customer-facing agent test pipelines must continually evolve as user distribution shifts, such as new products or entering new markets like Brazil and Argentina with different languages, policies and laws.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Agent QA is an ongoing operational expense, not a one-time project, supporting recurring-revenue testing platforms.
insights.locator: And the important part is if

insights.claim: User simulations through APIs can be run fully in parallel, while web-based simulations that drive a browser are slower and less parallelizable because only so many browsers can run on a machine.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: API-exposed agents are cheaper to test at scale than browser-based ones.
insights.locator: Running Simulations in Parallel

insights.claim: Arklex offers an open-source Python package, ArkSim, in which a user-simulator API talks to the developer's agent API to generate data and run evaluations, plus automatic batch scenario generation.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Open-source entry points are the go-to-market model for agent evaluation startups.
insights.locator: Getting Started With Simulations

insights.claim: Agent simulations can be used across the whole lifecycle: by product managers for prototyping, by engineers for unit, pressure, integration and regression tests before deployment, and in production for daily drift checks on critical services.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Broad lifecycle use expands the addressable market for agent-simulation tools.
insights.locator: Different Scenarios For Running Simulations

insights.claim: Zhou Yu says some teams run a small batch of simulation tests every day on critical agent services to detect drift, because third-party tools the agent calls may silently stop working.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Dependence on third-party tools and changing models creates continuous monitoring demand.
insights.quote: There might be some tools that just happen to not work anymore.
insights.locator: There are so many different tools

insights.claim: Agent tests should not be binary pass/fail but multi-metric, combining task completion with cost, efficiency, compliance and safety, with CI/CD thresholds set per metric for deployment readiness.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Cost and compliance metrics join accuracy as gating criteria for AI deployments.
insights.locator: Pass/Fail Test Grading May Be Inappropriate

insights.claim: Detailed logging of agent statements, tool calls and user responses provides an audit trail for compliance, such as verifying an agent never mentions a competitor or showing identical outcomes when only a user's attribute is changed to test for bias.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Simulation logs can serve as regulatory evidence of best-effort bias and compliance testing.
insights.locator: Logging for Compliance and Regulation

insights.claim: Zhou Yu says the feature everyone wants is self-evolving agents that read failure reports, propose changes, rerun simulations and iterate on their own, with root-cause ranking of failures by impact.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Closed-loop auto-remediation is the next product frontier for agent ops platforms.

insights.claim: Synthetic data from simulated users can be used to fine-tune models to reduce cost, creating a data flywheel for self-evolving agents without waiting for real user data.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Synthetic-data fine-tuning could lower inference costs by enabling smaller specialized models.
insights.locator: So you have stricter rules for it.

insights.claim: Zhou Yu argues QA spending is flipping: where QA was perhaps 2-5% of total spend, many teams building agents now spend a large share of time on evaluation because without standards you cannot optimize.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: A rising share of AI budgets going to evaluation favors agent testing and observability vendors.
insights.quote: Previously, you always thought quality assurance, a QA team is maybe 5% or 2% of your entire spend.
insights.locator: So evaluations are getting more and more

insights.claim: Zhou Yu argues that as LLMs grow more powerful and agents receive more autonomy, more evaluation is needed to control and verify them, especially as models change constantly and third-party tooling can fail.
insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Evaluation demand scales with agent autonomy, a structural tailwind for the category.

insights.speaker: Zhou Yu
insights.so_what: Points to platform consolidation in agent evaluation and possible standard-setting.

insights.so_what: Simulation fidelity is the main risk to the value of synthetic agent testing.
